question: If the angle subtended by arc AB at the center is 140°, what is the reflex angle made by this arc at the center?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total angle at the center of a full circle is 360°.

Reflex angle = Total angle − Given angle at center

Reflex angle = 360° − 140° = 220°

**∴ The correct answer is 220°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Reflex Angle = 220°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Reflex Angle

A reflex angle is strictly greater than 180° and strictly less than 360°. It represents the larger outer angle between two lines extending from a central point.

Complete Angle

The total angle swept around a single point or the center of a circle forms a complete angle, which is always equal to exactly 360°.

Angle Subtended by Arc Property

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle's circumference.
